subject: general
question: An agent sells a turbo cooker with a marked price of ₹6,370 at a discount of 60%. What is the selling price (in ₹) of the turbo cooker?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (100 − Discount)%

Since the discount is 60%, the agent sells the item at 40% of its Marked Price.

SP = 40% of 6370

SP = 637 × 4 = 2548

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,548.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 MP = ₹6370
 
• 
 

 −60% Discount
 
 SP = ?
 SP is 40% of MP (100% − 60%)

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) of the turbo cooker = ₹6,370

Discount offered = 60%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 6370 × (100 − 60) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 6370 × (40 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP = 6370 × 0.4

⇒ SP = 2548

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,548.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is a reduction offered on the Marked Price of an article to attract buyers. It is always calculated on the MP, not on the Cost Price (CP).

Successive Discounts

When two continuous discounts of x% and y% are given on an item, the equivalent single discount % = (x + y − xy ÷ 100)%.

Relationship between CP and MP

When both Profit% and Discount% are known, the direct ratio is calculated as: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).
